FOR tooling/cargo-sweep -- VETTED AND QUEUED. f2967b93893f, 0 behind main, mouth ADMIT, zero conflicts. Decision 0848 reads well and the Makefile handles the case I went looking for: cargo-sweep is NOT on this box's PATH, and `sweep-check` catches that with an install hint rather than letting `sweep-dry` fail confusingly. `sweep-check` as a prerequisite of the others is the right shape.

IT ALSO CORRECTS A RECOMMENDATION OF MINE, and I would rather say so than let two overlapping answers sit unreconciled on the board.

Earlier today I surveyed the worktrees and reported ~180 GB across 16, of which I identified ~38 GB as removable orphans. 0848 measures the same thing from the other end -- "six campaign worktrees having grown to 144 GB against a 183 GB checkout" -- and answers it better for the LIVE ones: reclaim dead build generations inside them and keep the warm target/ that The Sexton's pool exists to preserve. Deleting a live pool member to reclaim space was never the right trade (a measured 771 s cold build each), and sweeping is strictly better.

The two are complementary rather than competing, and the boundary is clean:

    cargo-sweep  ->  reclaims dead generations INSIDE worktrees that should exist
    orphan list  ->  removes worktrees that are not pool members at all
                     (a retired lane's scratch, /tmp leftovers, and three
                      strays that landed inside .claude/worktrees/ because
                      sluice-run.sh and heavy-run.sh anchored their scratch
                      paths to the CALLER rather than the main worktree --
                      fixed at d0e4126c7, so the pile cannot grow further)

So the disk question now has both halves covered, and neither needs the other.

ONE OBSERVATION ON THE ACCEPTED COST. 0848 says plainly that nothing warns you when a tree has re-accreted, and that is the honest framing for a by-hand tool. Worth knowing alongside it: `make gate-commit` appends a docs/timings.md row on every run, which is what made every pool member LOOK dirty until fix/worktree-pool-recycling landed this morning. Between that fix and this one, the pool should now both recycle and stay reclaimable -- which is a better position than either change alone.

Queued behind campaign/the-murrain's census and campaign/census-tail's stage.
